chunks: And those of your women who commit the indecency, call for four of you as witnesses against them; if they testify, then confine them in the houses until death takes them or Allah provides for them a way.

key_terms.الْفَاحِشَة: The indecency (specifically zina/fornication in this context)
key_terms.سَبِيلًا: A way (an alternative ruling or exemption)
key_terms.فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ: Then confine them / hold them back
key_terms.فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا: Then call for witnesses / seek testimony
key_terms.نِسَائِكُمْ: Your women (specifically unmarried women in this ruling)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment and procedure for unmarried women committing indecency according to this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this verse (Ayat al-Li'an contextually linked) is often interpreted as addressing unmarried women or serving as the initial ruling before the specific penalty for married adulterers was revealed, emphasizing the necessity of four eyewitnesses for major indecency. The confinement ('imdad') in homes reflects the pre-Islamic and early Islamic social structure, while the phrase 'until death or until Allah makes a way for them' allows for flexibility in legal application, such as exile or lighter penalties, as seen in the Hadith of the Twelve Imams.
